# 2 GENERAL INFORMATION

## 2.1 COURSE DESCRIPTION

Introduces the principles of lean thinking in modern production systems; philosophical, managerial and organizational requirements studied; lean manufacturing quantitative modeling methodologies, lean production cell design and case study analysis.

2.2 PREREQUISITES

ISEN 609 or by approval of instructor.

## 2.3 LEARNING OBJECTIVES

A lean production system (LPS) is one that generates goods and services with minimal buffering of products and resources. Systems engineering provides a compendium of methods and models to represent and characterize the complex nature of production systems and their interdependencies. The course is architected to expose the students to the knowledge, skills, and experiences (KSEs) of lean engineering supported by systems thinking.

The core principles of lean production systems are summarized as value, value stream, flow, control, and perfection. The lectures and class discussions have been organized around these 5-core principles. Like most systems, the LPS requires maintenance or it decays. The principle of perfection alludes to the never ending drive towards the 'lean production system upon a hill' - that is, true single-piece flow and quantity control enabled through quality control. But it is during LPS design that we must

instrument for waste accounting and PS 'health' monitoring. 6 σ ( variability reduction) is intrinsic to LPS design. Upon the completion of this course, the student will know how to:

- Represent a System of interest using SE architecture, lean methods, and tools.

- Analyze and Design, using SE and factory physics methods and tools, a production system with minimal buffering.

- Leverage 6 σ methods, tools, and techniques to reduce variation in both existing and proposed systems operations.

- Architect, using SE methods, an organization that is congruent with a lean-6 σ culture.

## 2.4 EXPECTATIONS

This is a course in Lean Engineering and students will not only learn how to think in terms of Lean but will also have a 'hands on' experience by working on practical exercises. Students will be placed in teams of 2-3 students, and each team will work the exercise to reinforce lean concepts. The teams will apply lean engineering to analyze manufacturing issues to address the problem.

## 2.5 COMMUNICATION AND MEETING TIMES

Communication will be via Canvas and via email. Students are expected to log onto the course daily and should carefully read all announcements and emails in their entirety. Course assignments needing grading will be submitted through Canvas, unless instructed otherwise. Students are expected to attend lectures in person.

2.6 COURSE MATERIAL AVAILABILITY

Course lecture materials will be provided for this course.
